context.verdict: The adapter LOSES to TF-IDF + logistic regression by 7.7 points micro / 12.6 macro.

diagnosis: Not a format failure: exact_label_rate is 1.000, every output is a valid class.
Not label noise: zero identical texts carry different priorities across 9,879 unique rows.
Not unlearnable: TF-IDF reaches 0.5467, well above the 0.3333 chance line.
The signal ceiling is genuinely low. Even TF-IDF is near-random on 'medium' (F1 0.52) and its best class is 'high' at 0.59.

Corroborating evidence from the rejected source: the CC0 Kaggle dataset predicted priority from customer_tier, error_rate_pct, downtime_min and security_incident_flag - account and incident METADATA, not wording. Its designers did not believe priority was a text problem either. Our result is the same conclusion reached empirically.
open_question: Whether the adapter's shortfall against TF-IDF is fixable (rank, learning rate, the ~2-token supervision signal per example after prompt masking) or whether a 1.5B decoder is simply the wrong tool for a 3-class problem with weak lexical signal. Untested.
